deterministic_checks.notes: All body citations resolve ([4a], [4a-sess] and [16] are defined inside the [4] and [16] entries; [E1]-[E6] in the last entry). Every References entry is cited. The only check mark without a footnote is line 339, in a role 6 section. All external sources are tier A rank 1, so no quarantine breach. sections_present is false because no heading does role 1 or role 4.

claim_checks.claim: It removed the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions
claim_checks.page_says: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport. ... Make MCP stateless: remove the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake.
claim_checks.note: Both removals are listed under Major changes of the 2026-07-28 changelog.

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.5 Current lifecycle (2026-07-28): no handshake
claim_checks.claim: A request missing a required key is rejected with `-32602`, and with HTTP 400 on HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: A request missing any required field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params). On HTTP, the response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: The required fields are the protocolVersion and clientCapabilities _meta keys in the table just above the passage.

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.5 Current lifecycle (2026-07-28): no handshake
claim_checks.claim: On HTTP there is nothing to shut down: each request is its own POST
claim_checks.page_says: Each request is its own POST ... HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405 Method Not Allowed.
claim_checks.note: The second half is stated. The page has no shutdown rule at all (searched 'shut', 'terminat'); what it supports is narrower: no session and no DELETE to end one. Open streams still have to be ended, for example a subscriptions/listen stream, which the client ends by closing it ([15], Cancellation). 'Nothing to shut down' widens 'no session to terminate'.

claim_checks.section: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle > ### 1.6 End-to-end session in six steps
claim_checks.claim: `notifications/tools/list_changed`, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection (legacy column, step 5)
claim_checks.page_says: The client MAY issue an HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint. ... or else return HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: Checked against the 2025-11-25 pages in [4] (the row is labelled legacy). On HTTP the GET stream exists only if the client opens one and the server offers one (it may answer 405); the row gives it as the delivery path with that condition dropped. The method name itself appears in [4a-sess] (notifications/tools/list_changed sent as server sent events).

claim_checks.section: ## 2. Q2: Primitives > ### 2.1 Server primitives (who controls them)
claim_checks.claim: A missing resource is error `-32602` in 2026-07-28 (it was `-32002` before; clients should still accept `-32002`)
claim_checks.page_says: If the requested resource does not exist, servers MUST return a JSON-RPC error with code -32602 (Invalid Params). ... clients SHOULD also accept -32002 as a resource not found error
claim_checks.note: [3] also records the change from -32002 to -32602 (SEP-2164).

claim_checks.claim: The client gathers the input and retries the original request with a new `id`, `inputResponses` and the echoed `requestState`
claim_checks.page_says: the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request. ... The JSON-RPC id MUST be different between the initial request and the retry
claim_checks.note: Line 193 of the page also gives the gather-then-retry step; InputResponses is defined at line 236.

claim_checks.claim: Worked example (2026-07-28, from the spec): `tools/call` id 2 returns an `input_required` result asking for a GitHub username via form elicitation; the client retries `tools/call` as id 3 with `inputResponses: {"github_login":{"action":"accept","content":{"name":"octocat"}}}` and the same `requestState`
claim_checks.note: The tools page example has response id 2, retry id 3 and the same requestState value in both.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.1 The standard transports
claim_checks.claim: optional `MCP-Session-Id`; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client `DELETE` to end (2025-11-25 column, Sessions row)
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: Optional session and 404 after termination (MUST) are supported. '400 without it' is a SHOULD written as a plain statement and drops the condition 'servers that require a session ID'; 'client DELETE to end' is a SHOULD, and the server MAY answer that DELETE with 405.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.4 Choosing a transport
claim_checks.claim: Existing HTTP+SSE server: keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: Servers wanting to support older clients should: Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint”

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.4 Choosing a transport
claim_checks.claim: Need server push of tool-list changes: `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) or GET stream (legacy)
claim_checks.page_says: It replaces the former resources/subscribe RPC and the HTTP GET endpoint. ([15]) ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream. ([4], 2025-11-25 transports)
claim_checks.note: A recommendation of which mechanism to use, and each page offers that mechanism for its era.

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.5 Authorization for HTTP servers (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: The modal matches, but the qualifier 'security' is dropped, which widens the rule to all best practice; the page also scopes the list with 'When supported:' (when authorization is supported).

claim_checks.section: ## 3. Q3: Transports and authorization > ### 3.5 Authorization for HTTP servers (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. ... insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: ... HTTP 403 Forbidden status code
claim_checks.note: Token validation, audience check and 401 are MUST and entail. The 403 / insufficient_scope / scope part is SHOULD on the page (and 'servers SHOULD include the scopes needed'), but it sits under the item's leading 'Server must' and under the flow's 'steps are normative unless marked': a SHOULD raised to MUST level.

claim_checks.section: ## 4. Q4: Security and trust > ### 4.2 Requirements by actor (2026-07-28)
claim_checks.claim: Resources: servers must validate URIs and sanitize `file://` paths against traversal
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate all resource URIs ... Servers MUST sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal attacks when serving file:// resources

claim_checks.section: ## 4. Q4: Security and trust > ### 4.4 Confused deputy
claim_checks.claim: SSRF through metadata URLs (clients should require HTTPS and block private ranges, and use an egress proxy on servers)
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients SHOULD require HTTPS for all OAuth-related URLs in production environments ... operators SHOULD consider using an egress proxy that enforces network policies
claim_checks.note: 'should block private ranges' entails. 'should use an egress proxy' raises 'SHOULD consider using' short of MUST, and the HTTPS rule drops 'in production environments'. The item's own 'should' governs it, although the sentence opens with 'Related attacks with required mitigations'.

claim_checks.section: ## 5. What the experiments showed that the spec text does not say
claim_checks.claim: v1 SDK has no `server/discover`; its `initialize` negotiated an unknown version down to 2025-11-25 (E2)
claim_checks.page_says: not found: the claim cites only local experiment E2, which has no saved text in INPUT
claim_checks.note: The check mark carries no [..] footnote, only '(E2)' in prose. Also, no experiment listed in section 6 sends server/discover to the v1 SDK (E2 tested version negotiation only), so the first half has no named backing at all.
